question.problem: Find the equation of the level surface for the function $f(x,y,z)={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-z$ that passes through the point $P(0,-2,4).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,2,4) & ={2}^{2}-{0}^{2}-4 \\  & =4-0-4 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-z & =0 \\ z & ={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface that passes through the point $P(0,-2,4)$ is the hyperbolic paraboloid $z={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}.$
